blocks.text: Follow-up call with Odile Wickley and Gwen Rushton of Quadling Health Access.

Odile reports that planning for the mobile vaccination clinic in North Orchard's community hall is underway. She is focusing on securing the necessary permissions from the hall's trustees and arranging for a reliable power supply. She says the hall's existing outlets are insufficient for the clinic's equipment, so she is exploring options with a local electrician.
The trustees meet next week. I’ll present the proposal then. The electrician said it should be straightforward to run a dedicated line from the panel.

Gwen reported on her recent work. After learning two regular transport volunteers would be away over the Gloomglow holiday, she compiled a list of on-call backup drivers. She confirmed availability with each one and updated the dispatch schedule.

It took a few days of calls, but we lined up four reliable people. Because of that, we didn’t have to cancel the three trips we had scheduled for the 24th, 26th, and 27th. All three patients got to their appointments.

Odile mentioned she will reach out to the Meadow Mutual Aid circle to see if they have experience with similar clinic setups. Gwen noted she’d be happy to share her backup driver protocol with other circles if they find it useful.
